items.question: What is EmDash?
items.answer: EmDash is an Astro-native CMS with a full admin panel. You model content in the admin, and your Astro site queries it. It deploys to Cloudflare Workers or to a Node.js server.

items.question: Do I need Cloudflare to run EmDash?
items.answer: No. Cloudflare Workers with D1 and R2 is one option. EmDash also runs on Node.js with SQLite and local file storage, for example on a VPS. The EmDash review on bitdoze.com compares both.

items.question: Are the themes and plugins listed here free?
items.answer: Each listing carries a Free or Paid badge. Paid entries show the price and link to the seller's page.

items.question: Who runs this site?
items.answer: I'm Dragos. I write the guides at bitdoze.com and publish the videos on the Bitdoze YouTube channel.

data.title: Stopping contact form spam with Cloudflare Turnstile
data.excerpt: The contact form plugin gained an invisible Turnstile challenge: how it works, what changed in 1.1.0, and the cache gotcha to avoid.

children.text: The contact form on this site started attracting spam within days of going live — SEO pitches, link drops, the usual. The form plugin already had a honeypot, a minimum-fill-time check and an hourly IP limit. Bots that post directly to the endpoint skipped all three.
We added Cloudflare Turnstile: a checkbox-free challenge that browsers solve in the background and the server verifies before anything is stored or emailed.
What was already there
Three passive defenses came with the plugin:

items.text: Honeypot field — hidden from humans, filled by bots
Minimum fill time — instant posts get silently accepted but dropped
Per-IP hourly limit — 20 submissions per address per hour

children.text: They catch the lazy bots. They miss the ones that render the page, take their time, or rotate through a botnet of addresses.
Adding Turnstile

Two settings on the plugin — a site key and an encrypted secret — switch the whole thing on. The form route exposes the site key, the component renders the widget, and the submit route verifies the token against Cloudflare's siteverify endpoint before storing anything.

Pages are edge-cached. If you enable Turnstile on a cached page that was rendered without the widget, visitors post without a token and get challenged. Redeploy to clear the cache after saving the keys.

body.quote: The best challenge is the one a real visitor never has to see.

data.title: A widgets plugin for EmDash articles
data.excerpt: Nineteen new block types — notices, tabs, product boxes, a table of contents and a live latest-posts list — usable on posts and pages.

children.text: Most of what this site publishes is a list of links — tutorials that live on bitdoze.com, videos that live on YouTube. The blog is different: full articles that live here, built from the same block editor the pages use.
To make that work we built a small plugin, Content Widgets, that adds nineteen widget_* block types. Editors drop them into any blocks field — this post's body is made of them.
Every widget below is a block in this post's body field. Open it in the admin to see the editing experience.
What's in the box

items.text: Notice — info, success, warning and danger callouts
Accordion and Tabs — collapsible and tabbed sections
YouTube, Embed, Product box and Facts table
Table of contents, Series nav and Latest posts

children.text: Install it
The plugin is on the EmDash registry. After install, copy the block types into your schema and the components into your site — the setup guide page in the admin walks through it.

items.label: npm
items.body:
npm install emdashhq-widgets

Then register it under sandboxed: in astro.config.mjs and copy the site/ files as described in the setup guide.

items.label: bun
items.body:
bun add emdashhq-widgets

Then register it under sandboxed: in astro.config.mjs and copy the site/ files as described in the setup guide.

data.title: How the blog section works on this site
data.excerpt: A posts collection, one route, and the widget blocks doing double duty — the anatomy of this site's new blog.

children.text: This site gained a blog this week. Not a separate system — a posts collection, one route, and the widget blocks from the new Content Widgets plugin. Here's how it fits together.
A posts collection, not pages

Posts live in their own collection with title, excerpt, cover, featured and a blocks body. The collection's urlPattern (/blog/{slug}) is what the Latest posts widget uses to resolve links — the route that renders them is src/pages/blog/[slug].astro.
Blocks instead of one long body
A post body is a list of blocks. Prose blocks carry the rich text; widgets slot between them. It's the same editor the marketing pages use, so nothing new to learn.

items.title: Why blocks instead of Portable Text?
items.body: Sandboxed plugins can't register custom Portable Text block types — that's a trusted-plugin feature. A blocks field gets the same result with a schema the site controls, and the widgets also work on regular pages.

items.title: How does the posts list stay fresh?
items.body: widget_latest_posts calls the plugin's public posts route in-process at render time — no HTTP fetch, no build step. The route reads published entries ordered by publish date.

items.title: Do widgets work on pages too?
items.body: Yes. Every widget_* type is allowed on the pages content field as well as the posts body, so a landing page can use a notice or a product box.

data.title: The widget gallery — every block in one post
data.excerpt: A kitchen-sink tour of all nineteen Content Widgets blocks: callouts, tabs, steps, code, product boxes, cards, quotes and more.

children.text: This post exists to show what the Content Widgets plugin can do. Every block type it ships appears here exactly once, in the order an editor would meet them in the admin picker.
Prose is the plain block between everything else — a rich text field with headings, lists and inline links.
Callouts
Notices call something out without breaking the reading flow:
A neutral note — background context, prerequisites, a version requirement.
The thing you just did worked. Confirm it before moving on.
Careful — this step is easy to get wrong.
Do not do this on production data. Destructive and hard to undo.
Folding content away

items.title: Do widgets work on pages too?
items.body: Yes — any blocks field can allow the widget_ types. This site allows them on pages and on posts.

items.title: What about the table of contents?
items.body: It scans the rendered h2 and h3 headings in the browser and links to them. No config needed.

items.title: Can I restyle the widgets?
items.body: Every component uses wgt- classes and falls back to plain CSS values when the site does not define the theme tokens.

items.label: npm
items.body: npm install emdashhq-widgets — then register the plugin in astro.config.mjs under sandboxed.

items.label: pnpm
items.body: pnpm add emdashhq-widgets — same registration step afterwards.

items.label: Registry
items.body: Or install from the EmDash plugin registry in the admin: Plugins, Add plugin, search Content Widgets.
